c.v: Built-up roofing (BUR)

runs.v: is a low-slope membrane that alternates layers of reinforcing fabric and hot bitumen on the deck, then surfaces the plies with gravel, mineral granules, or a reflective coating that shields the membrane from UV and impact. Another name for built-up roofing is tar-and-gravel roofing. Gravel-surfaced BUR is finished with a flood coat of hot asphalt and embedded rock aggregate, which is naturally non-combustible, so aggregate-surfaced systems earn high fire ratings that help satisfy local building codes; smooth-surfaced BUR trades the gravel for a smooth asphalt coating or a modified bitumen cap sheet, which is easier to inspect.

sections.heading: Built-Up Roofing vs. Asphalt Shingles and Metal Roofing on Bloomfield Homes

c.v: Are built-up roofs better than shingles?

runs.v: On a flat or low-slope roof, yes: asphalt shingles need a slope of at least 2:12 under the International Residential Code, while BUR is built for low slopes and gives long-term value there. On the pitched roofs of Bloomfield homes, shingles win, and roofing materials there include asphalt, slate, and metal systems: asphalt shingles last 20 to 30 years in Bloomfield, standing seam metal and other metal roofs 40 to 80 years, and slate 60 to 150 years, per the InterNACHI chart. Newark Quality Roofing installs GAF Timberline, Owens Corning, and CertainTeed shingles with balanced attic ventilation; whichever roofing material an owner in Bloomfield chooses, the slope decides the system.

c.v: Pitched Bloomfield homes

runs.v: show their own wear: ridge caps on Dutch Colonials often show damage after 20 to 30 years, the rubber roof sections on split-level homes typically fail after 20 to 25 years, and ice dams form on Craftsman homes because wide eave overhangs stay colder than the roof over the heated walls.

c.v: What are the disadvantages of a built-up roof?

runs.v: Weight, because gravel surfacing adds load the framing must carry; fumes and odor from hot-mopped installation in an occupied building; slower roof installation than single-ply systems; and leaks that are harder to trace once water travels between the plies.

sections.heading: Roof Repair, Emergency Roof Repair, or Complete Roof Replacement?

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: As a rule of thumb, once damage covers about 25% of a roof, a complete roof replacement usually costs less over time than repeated roof repair, and on a flat roof the line sits at 25–30% of the membrane; a full replacement involves stripping the roof to the deck. As a permit rule, N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 requires a construction permit when more than 25% of a commercial, multi-family, or attached building's roof is repaired or replaced within 12 months, while reroofing a detached one- or two-family house is ordinary maintenance.

runs.v: requests are triaged for active leaks first: a temporary patch or tarp stops the water, and the permanent repair or new roof follows once the roof is dry.
